name: Snap score
seoDesc: Snap score: a free health calculator that walks you through 29 values, with the formula spelled out and a worked example.
summary: The Snap score calculator is a free, no-sign-up health tool. Fill in the 26 fields it asks for and it works out inattention Subset straight away, with the formula shown underneath. Think of it as a shortcut for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Nothing repaints underneath you: edit a field, press Calculate, and the new answer appears. That is how you find out which input the result is sensitive to.

sections.title: How does the Snap score calculator work?
sections.html:
The Snap score calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports inattention Subset in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities., the often fidgets with hands or feet or squirms in seat. and the often talks excessively.).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

sections.title: The formula behind the Snap score calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Inattention Subset=(often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes in schoolwork or tasks. + often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities. + often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly. + often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties. + often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities. + often avoids, dislikes, or reluctantly engages in tasks requiring sustained mental effort. + often loses things necessary for activities (e.g., toys, school assignments, pencils or books). + often is distracted by extraneous stimuli. + often is forgetful in daily activities.)
Hyperactivity / Impulsivity Subset=(often fidgets with hands or feet or squirms in seat. + often leaves seat in classroom or in other situations in which remaining seated is expected. + often runs about or climbs excessively in situations in which it is inappropriate. + often has difficulty playing or engaging in leisure activities quietly. + often is “on the go” or often acts as if “driven by a motor.” + often talks excessively. + often blurts out answers before questions have been completed. + often has difficulty awaiting their turn. + often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations ÷ games).)
Opposition / Defiance Subset=(often loses temper. + often argues with adults. + often actively defies or refuses adult requests or rules. + often deliberately does things that annoy other people. + often blames others for his or her mistakes or misbehavior. + often is touchy or easily annoyed by others. + often is angry and resentful. + often is spiteful or vindictive.)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Snap score calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

sections.title: Which calculators go with this one?
sections.html: If this one is part of a bigger problem, these health calculators cover the neighbouring steps: Pediatric epinephrine dose, Pediatric Epworth sleepiness scale and Pediatric GFR (glomerular filtration rate).

faq.q: What does the Snap score calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns inattention Subset. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Snap score calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 26 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (26 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Inattention Subset = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Snap score calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
